THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 17.01.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.2763/2018 ON THE FILE OF THE XIX ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, MACT, BENGALURU (SCCH-17), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS MFA COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant is in appeal challenging the finding of the Tribunal by which 10% of negligence has been attributed to the deceased and consequentially, a reduction of 10% in the compensation has been awarded.
2. The evidence on record indicates that the deceased was riding a motorcycle and the accident occurred when the car driven by respondent No.2 collided with him at a cross road.

The Tribunal Smt Chotimeena vs United India Insurance Company Ltd on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5413693/
2 has taken the view that the deceased could have avoided the car hitting the two wheeler and it therefore attributed negligence to the extent of 10%.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has also taken the view that the car had the driver reduced the speed and avoided overtaking of vehicle at a place where he was not supposed to do, the accident could have been easily avoided.

Since the Tribunal recorded a finding that the driver of the car was trying to overtake the vehicle at a place where he was not supposed to and also did not reduce speed, in my view, the attribution of 10% negligence on the deceased is improper.
It is also noticed here that a charge-sheet was also laid against the driver of the car.
This also points to the fact that there was no negligence on the part of the deceased.
Consequently, the finding of the Tribunal attributing negligence on the deceased at 10% is set-aside.

3. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 19,68,792/-

2 . Loss of Consortium 40,000/-
 Funeral expenses &
 3. 15,000/-
Transportation charges

4. Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Total 20,38,792/-
4.

In coming to this conclusion, the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.12,500/-
and added future prospect of 25%, in my view, this assessment of notional income and additional future prospects is just and proper and does not call for any interference.
5. However, it is noticed that though there were five claimants, only a sum of Rs.40,000/- has been awarded towards loss of consortium.

In the light of the judgment rendered in the MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. NANU RAM @ CHUHRU RAM - (2018) 18 SCC 130, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head "loss of consortium"
and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".
6.

The interest awarded by the Tribunal at 7.5% p.a. is modified and the claimants would be entitled to 6% interest on the entire compensation.

8. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to the total compensation of Rs.22,21,792/- as against Rs.20,38,792/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
9. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The modified compensation amount shall be apportioned and disbursed in terms of the order of the Tribunal.
The appeal filed by the claimants is allowed-in- part.
